items.title: Cyclic Partition
items.summary: Partitioning with nearly one assignment per moved value, instead of Hoare's one and a half By Tigran Hayrapetyan Project page: https://towardsdatascience.com/cyclic-partition/ ShipAI is a Towards Data Science project. Watch all the videos here: https://towardsdatascience.com/videos/ Key takeaways. 1. Hoare's scheme swaps misplaced values in pairs, costing three assignments per two, or 1.5 per value. 2. Cyclic partition chains the moves through emptied slots: L displaced values take only L+1 assignments. 3. On integers both run about the same; on large objects the cyclic version pulls ahead as more values move. items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Beyond the Demo: How Oracle and Deloitte Are Putting AI Agents to Work
items.summary: While enterprise AI spent its first two years functioning as an intelligent search engine, autonomous agents are now being embedded directly into core ERP, HR, and supply chain applications to execute complex business decisions. Despite a Deloitte survey revealing that 74% of IT leaders expect to rebuild processes around AI agents within four years, only 5% feel fully prepared to deploy them safely. Moving from tightly controlled pilots to messy production environments requires establishing single data architectures, defining explicit guardrails for what agents must *not* do, and building human-in-the-loop orchestration layers. In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Madhukar Uniyal, Senior Director of Solutions Engineering at Oracle India, and Arvind Girotra, Partner at Deloitte India. They analyze the ground reality of enterprise agentic adoption, from invoice processing and shift handovers to HR query resolution. They explore the mechanics of Oracle Fusion Flow, mitigating cross-departmental agent conflicts, data model dependencies on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), managing employee workforce anxiety through reskilling into agent auditors, and evaluating the hard economics of agentic ROI. Are your internal data lakes and enterprise architectures ready to support autonomous agents, or are legacy silos holding back production scale? items.title: Agents Acting Safely on Our Behalf
items.summary: What happens to the web when the ones browsing it are no longer people? Sarah Drasner, Area Tech Lead at Google, sits down with us ahead of her Agentic Web keynote at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America. She works through that question from both directions: rebuild the web so agents can use it properly, or build agents smart enough to handle the web as it already exists. We get into the split between computer-use and browser-use agents on one side and API and MCP agents on the other. We also watch a real example of the idea in action: an agent pulling speaker photos from Flickr, hunting down company logos, and loading everything into Canva so the human only touches the creative part. From there, Sarah shares the unlikely origin story of WebMCP (and who's to blame for it). We then pressure-test a bold idea: a WebMCP gateway that could cover the huge share of websites that will never ship support on their own. Along the way, we cover the instinct that separates senior engineers, the ability to sense which business problems are actually worth solving. We also talk about how thought experiments cut through a pile of competing priorities, the hacky WebMCP workarounds already showing up in the wild, and why the best agent experiences are the ones that delight customers in ways they never saw coming.
